display.purpose: The album's average rating. Display face and weight come from the theme.

headline.purpose: Album and screen titles in the theme's display face; 40px on wide screens.

title.purpose: Section heads such as listen later, november and tracklist.

body.purpose: The phone's base size for cells, rows and buttons.

label.purpose: Uppercase release facts with tabular numerals, led by a series square.

shadows.name: glass-light
shadows.purpose: Catalogue light glass drop shadow (each theme sets --glass-shadow).

shadows.name: glass-rim
shadows.purpose: Hairline rim on every glass surface.

shadows.name: glass-specular
shadows.purpose: Specular line along the top of every glass surface.

shadows.name: hero-cover
shadows.purpose: The album page's main cover only. Panels have no shadows.

motion.name: press
motion.value: transform 0.18s; scale(0.96) on buttons, scale(0.98) on the log block
motion.purpose: Press feedback standing in for haptics.

motion.name: tabbar-minimise
motion.purpose: Tab pill and Log button size change when scrolling past about 120px.

motion.name: tab-fade
motion.purpose: Unselected tabs fade when the bar minimises.

motion.name: title-collapse
motion.purpose: Large title to inline title past about 44px of scroll.

motion.name: haptic-bounce
motion.value: to be confirmed in the screen ticket
motion.purpose: Star bounce on rating (story 33) and bookmark bounce on listen later (story 57). Intent only, not in the reference build.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: Tab bar, Log button, inline title and scroll-edge fade change state instantly.

narrative.overview:
auxo dresses like a record label's house style: an exact, quiet frame of type and numbers that presents every cover the same way, so the artwork changes and the frame never does. Cool paper grey and ink, one ultramarine for actions and selection, heavy system sans with tight tracking, tabular numbers, and small uppercase spec lines. The covers carry all the colour; the frame stays still.

The frame borrows the iPhone's own grammar (large titles, floating glass bars, grouped panels, sheets) because auxo should feel like a first-party app on the phone it lives on. It refuses the streaming-store page (big tinted hero, carousels of carousels) and the rating-site table.

Catalogue is the default look. Sleeve and Standard are themes people pick in Settings (ADR [0009](docs/adr/0009-selectable-themes-catalogue-default.md)). A theme swaps tokens only: palette, star colour, glass tint, display face and corner radii. Layout, components and motion are shared, so a screen is designed and tested once and checked in all three themes, light and dark.
keyCharacteristics: One frame for every cover: the artwork changes, the frame doesn't.
Ink and paper with a single ultramarine for actions and selection.
Spec lines: 11px uppercase, 0.06em tracking, tabular numbers, a series colour square.
Ink stars in Catalogue, not gold.
Floating glass for bars, controls and the sidebar only.
Light and dark follow the system in every theme.

rules.name: The One Blue Rule
rules.body: Ultramarine marks what you can do and what is selected. It is never decoration, never a background wash, and never a second accent beside another.

rules.name: The Series Rule
rules.body: Series colours mean album type and nothing else. They don't change with the theme, and they only appear as the small square in a spec line.

rules.name: The Token Rule
rules.body: Every colour, radius and display face in a component comes from a theme token.

rules.name: The Tabular Rule
rules.body: Ratings, counts, dates, durations and track numbers use tabular numerals so they line up down a column.

rules.name: The Spec Line Rule
rules.body: Facts about a release (type, year, genres, relisten) go in an uppercase 11px spec line led by its series square, never in a sentence.

rules.name: The Clear Cover Rule
rules.body: Glass never sits on album artwork. The album page's floating controls sit on the ground above the cover, and the cover starts below them. auxo must not feel like frosted chrome over the artwork.

rules.name: The Finished Fallback Rule
rules.body: The blur-and-tint glass is the design. Refraction is a bonus for some browsers, never a fix for a fallback that looks unfinished.

dos: Do take every colour, radius and display face from a theme token, and check each screen in all three themes, light and dark.
Do keep ultramarine for actions and selection only.
Do put release facts in a spec line with its series square.
Do use tabular numerals for every rating, count, date and duration.
Do make the blur-and-tint glass look finished before adding refraction.
Do honour reduced motion and reduced transparency.
Do give every album without artwork the placeholder cover.
donts: Don't put glass on album artwork.
Don't use glass for panels, cards or content; it is for bars, controls and the sidebar.
Don't change layout, components or motion per theme.
Don't recolour the wordmark or icon for a theme, or capitalise auxo.
Don't use Apple logos, trademarks, the Apple Music name or SF Symbols artwork.
Don't use gold stars in Catalogue; its stars are ink.
Don't use series colours for anything but album type.
